title: Confound in my dividing-crawler claim: the finite-range term's negative branch is a content-independent growth drive; without it the founder starves, with it starved bodies never die
summary: In 20261025T0828-c04-crawler-divide-claim the finite-range term lamOK/V0 (G*u - Mref V0) is negative for any body smaller than the kernel scale, lowering delta by up to lamOK*Mref = 1.2 and so pushing small bodies to grow regardless of their content. Two tests on seeds 1 and 2 (world.py here; switches bV, okclip, t_starve). (a) With actin production scaled by content (bV=1) and all food removed at t=300, content V reaches 0 in every body, yet 15 and 16 bodies persist to t=600 as diffuse bumps (u max 0.86, |P| 0; bV_starve/ghost_probe.txt): delta inside them is about 0.5 + 0.7 - 0.9 = 0.3, held below 1/2 by the negative branch. (b) Clipping the term at 0 (okclip=1, penalty only for oversized bodies) kills the founder in full food by t~90 on both seeds (okclip_fed/): uptake (~15/time) cannot pay the shedding cost of a crawler moving at ~2/time (~24/time), which the negative branch had masked by letting area run ahead of content. So the claim's viability and its absence of starvation deaths both rest on this drive. The I, M, D observations stand, but the growth is partly by construction, and the world shows no metabolism (L4c). tools/crawler.py is included so that tools/post.py (also in 20261025T0849) imports.

finding.operator: finite-range (Gaussian kernel) area penalty with offset Mref
finding.control: clip the term at 0 (okclip=1); starvation fork with content-dependent actin (bV=1)
finding.result: clipped: founder dies by t~90 in full food (2/2 seeds); unclipped and starved: V=0 in all bodies but 15/16 persist to t=600
